result.question: Give me a sample-by-sample picture of the fault gases in Transformer 1 at MAIN between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. For each sample, list hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Name the dominant gas, meaning the one with the highest ppm, and give its percentage of the five-gas total. Then tell me whether the dominant gas changed at any point in the window. Say what that shift points to, for example hydrogen pointing to partial discharge, ethylene to a hotter thermal fault, or acetylene to arcing. Also rank the five gases by their percentage growth from the first to the last sample. If a gas is null in a sample, leave it out of that sample's total and mark it as missing. If fewer than two samples have all five gases, give the ranking from the latest reading alone and say that no trend could be established.
result.answer:
Transformer 1 at MAIN has 4 daily samples in the window, and all five gases are present in every one, so a trend can be worked out. Ethylene is the dominant gas in every sample at about 51.5% of the five-gas total.

| Timestamp | H₂ | CH₄ | C₂H₆ | C₂H₄ | C₂H₂ | 5-gas total | Dominant (% of total) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 00:00 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32409 | Ethylene (51.48%) |
| 2024-01-16 00:00 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 32056 | Ethylene (51.47%) |
| 2024-01-17 00:00 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 32308 | Ethylene (51.69%) |
| 2024-01-18 00:00 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 32307 | Ethylene (51.38%) |

All values are in ppm. No values are missing.

**Did the dominant gas change?** No. Ethylene stays on top in all 4 samples, between 51.4% and 51.7% of the total, so there is no shift to hydrogen (partial discharge) or acetylene (arcing). The gas pattern points to one ongoing fault: a hotter thermal fault, likely above 300°C. Methane and ethane are the next largest gases, which fits that picture. Acetylene stays at only 6–8 ppm, so arcing is unlikely. The fault gases are at very high levels overall but held steady across the four days.

**Ranking by growth from the first sample to the last:**
1. Hydrogen: 2845 → 2900, **+1.93%**
2. Acetylene: 7 → 7, **0.00%**
3. Ethane: 5467 → 5450, **−0.31%**
4. Ethylene: 16684 → 16600, **−0.50%**
5. Methane: 7406 → 7350, **−0.76%**

All changes are under 2%, which is within normal sampling noise, so no gas is clearly rising.
